plan: dispatch://INFRA-889/artifact/plan-md (v1). Twelve tasks: T1 base and the INFRA-771 check, T2 delete the port push, T3 delete the live topics lane, T4 refuse a registration naming a port, T5 warn and ignore the two variables, T6 the interest row names the current registration, T7 the per-file test disposition, T8 the scripts and their CI gate, T9 the two envoy-infra inputs, T10 documentation and the architecture component, T11 the pull request, T12 verification.

implement: skill://legion-worker — the phase contract, the shared workspace, the push and the handoff.

skill://legion-worker/references/cleanup-deletion.md — this change is a deletion of a feature with code, tests, scripts, Pulumi inputs, compose settings and documentation; the reference's rule is to complete the chain and resist opportunistic refactors, which is how T2-T10 are ordered.
skill://legion-worker/references/pr-body.md — the PR body template, what a proof is, and the simplify pass; T12 names the surface and command each proof runs on.

skill://legion-worker/references/conflicts-and-rewrites.md — sjawhar/legion#2603 (dispatch://INFRA-771) rewrites the same registration handler and mergeForUpsert; if it merges first, the base comes forward under this reference's rules.
skill://legion-worker/references/skip-checks-trailer.md — the handoff-only push carries the trailer and the code push does not.
skill://legion-worker/references/tools.md — the pod has no container runtime, so internal/smoke is read on GitHub while e2e-local.sh and the in-process nats-server run locally.
skill://ce-simplify-code — the implementer's one simplify pass, in the first implementing round.
skill://envoy — the delivery vocabulary this change rewrites in packages/envoy/AGENTS.md, skills/envoy/ and the docs site.
skill://dispatch and skill://plain-words — the Dispatch writes and the pull-request prose.
test: skill://legion-worker — the phase contract and the test handoff's shape.
skill://legion-worker/references/pr-body.md — verify the implementer's proof, then add the tester's own E2E line; a handoff with no proof is a test failure, not a gap for the tester to fill.
skill://legion-worker/references/tools.md — internal/smoke needs a container runtime the pod lacks; read envoy-smoke on GitHub and drive e2e-local.sh locally.
skill://envoy — the consumer delivery path the e2e session now receives on.
review: skill://legion-worker/references/merge-gate.md — the order from the tester's evidence to READY.
skill://legion-worker/references/cleanup-deletion.md — the completeness of a deletion is what this review judges, against the A3 grep.
skill://thermonuclear-deep-review and skill://thermonuclear-code-quality — the reviewer's pair.

findings.finding: F1 — A3 cannot pass as worded: its grep matches 61 files today, the spec's requirements name about 18, and the exclusion list misses packages/<pkg>/.changes/unreleased/*.yaml, where this repository's changelog fragments live, so a fragment naming the two variables would fail A3.
findings.answer: Every one of the 61 files is in T2-T10. The plan's section 'A3's machine-checkable form' states the corrected command: the spec's grep plus ':!**/.changes/**', and plus ':!packages/claude-envoy/dist/**' for the pre-merge run only. The permitted residue is named exactly: the warning in packages/envoy/cmd/listener/main.go and its test. No document and no golden names either variable. The change to an acceptance line is listed for the architect.

findings.finding: F2 — packages/envoy/internal/smoke/listener_test.go:205 registers {"port":8080} and asserts 200, and release-envoy-listener.yaml's docker job runs it (:237-238) before the image publishes (:246), so refusing a port blocks the image dispatch://INFRA-891 must pin. infra/core/permissions_live_test.go holds serving-port and SubscribeAllTopics scenarios in the same job.
findings.answer: T7's table names both files with their dispositions, and says the smoke test needs self_subscribed or a consumer delivery as well as port: 0, since the entry-write gate (cmd/listener/api.go:1511) otherwise leaves the session out of /v1/sessions. T12 records that internal/smoke is read on GitHub in envoy-smoke, and names the release docker job as the gate INFRA-891 depends on.

findings.finding: F3 — A1's '/v1/sessions answers port: 0 for it' holds only for a registration that writes a session entry; a bare port-0 registration writes none (cmd/listener/api.go:1511) and appears nowhere.
findings.answer: T7's new A1 test registers port: 0 with a consumer delivery. T4 narrows the entry-write gate to body.SelfSubscribed || delivery.relayed() and keeps sessionInfo.Port, which every released client parses.

findings.finding: F4 — R3 names no consumer client for e2e-local.sh; loadtest/relay.go is one file of the load generator's package main, @legion/envoy-client declares no bin, and a third go build in the script would need a matching script_run pin in .github/scripts/ci_job_reads.py.
findings.answer: D2 picks an inline bun -e NATS consumer stand-in and gives its whole contract (the deliver subject, the six headers, the received/done answers, the registration's delivery field, and the role-forward receipt the stand-in now answers itself). T8 keeps the two pinned go build texts untouched and refreshes the gate's stale why anchors.

findings.finding: F5 — Deliverer.Text dies with the push (its only non-test caller is Push, session.go:248), taking nine golden assertions and the Go half of e2e-local.sh's Go-vs-TS renderer comparison; the spec never mentions it.
findings.answer: D3 states it, with the reason that no second renderer is left to be out of step with, and T7 and T8 delete both sides. It is listed for the architect as a coverage decision and recorded as a spec departure.

findings.finding: F6 — R1 names pushFailedDeferrals and a push_failed reason; neither exists. Read literally it would delete unplaceableDeferrals, which is cause-agnostic and still serves no_session_record.
findings.answer: D4 gives a table of what is actually in the tree and what happens to each: unplaceableDeferrals and no_session_record stay; the no_push_target reason, the unplaceable_no_push_target label, session.ErrNoPushTarget, ReasonNoPushTarget and ReasonPushFailed go. No dashboard in this repository reads the dropped label.

findings.finding: F7 — R4 and the spec's Design sentence point at different code, and repointing senderStamp at the session entry leaves Registry.Match and durable.go:416-417 naming the first listener, so R4 stays unmet; it also empties sender.Machine for a registration that writes no entry and for a session whose 5-minute entry lapsed while its 15-minute interest row lives. A4's 'fails on main with INFRA-771 merged' is not runnable: #2603 is open.
findings.answer: D1 meets R4 at the write, in mergeForUpsert, and leaves every reader unchanged, with the evidence for why the alternative cannot work. The departure is recorded below and listed for the architect. T12 runs A4's red baseline on main as it stands, with #2446 alone.

findings.finding: F8 — hostBridge is a required input of aws:WebhookListener and a required flag of envoy-infra render; nobody had established whether a consumer outside this repository constructs those components.
findings.answer: Measured and recorded in the plan's 'Measured facts': theorem-labs/agent-infra's envoy/main.go constructs envoyinfra:gcp:NatsHub and envoyinfra:nats only; the two inputs appear there solely in the vendored generated SDK, and its in-cluster listener sets ENVOY_SUBSCRIBE_ALL_TOPICS=1 as a plain corev1.EnvVar (envoy-cluster/listener.go:129), which R2's warn-and-ignore covers until dispatch://INFRA-891. T9 carries the deletion, the four goldens and the schema assertion.

findings.finding: F9 — 'the Go tests that observed delivery through a fake port observe it through a session consumer instead' has two readings: convert every file, or delete the ones whose subject is the port.
findings.answer: T7 is a per-file disposition table with the rule stated: a test whose subject is delivery is converted; a test whose subject is the port mechanism is deleted, because it has no subject left.

findings.finding: F10 — no acceptance proves this change on a production-like surface, and the spec never says what the implementer's production check may claim, since no production listener runs the change until dispatch://INFRA-891 moves the pins.
findings.answer: D7 names the production-like surface inside this change (scripts/e2e-local.sh: a listener binary from the checkout, a real nats-server, real webhook fixtures, a session on its own consumer, and no container runtime) and the sentence the production check will say: pending, naming dispatch://INFRA-891 as what carries the change to production. That is the daemon's own supported state, not a deferral.

findings.finding: F11 — the spec's '0 of 601 sessions with a port on 2026-10-31' is a dated one-off reading nothing re-checks, and the instruction to tell INFRA-771's implementer needed a live holder.
findings.answer: Re-measured: GET /v1/sessions on the in-cluster listener at $ENVOY_URL on 2026-11-02T07:12:55Z gave 377 sessions, 0 with port > 0; recorded in the plan's 'Measured facts'. T1 makes the message to notifications.role.legion-infra-infra-771-implementer a task with the exact file list.

findings.finding: F12 — answered, not findings: .dispatch/architecture/envoy-listener.md must change in the same review; deleting the ENVOY_SUBSCRIBE_ALL_TOPICS refusal is safe in either rollout direction; old listener with a new client is a non-event; envoy-session-stall registers no serve port; ci_job_reads.py's why anchors are free text.
findings.answer: T10 carries the architecture component file. T5 follows envDuration's warn-and-continue convention. T8 refreshes the stale why anchors and keeps the two pinned go build texts, which are what the gate compares.

specDepartures.spec: Design: "For R4, the plan names every reader of the interest row's machine id and directory left after the deletion, and removes it or makes it read the session entry."
specDepartures.plan: R4 is met at the write instead: packages/envoy/internal/store/kv.go:682-699 (mergeForUpsert) takes the registration's own MachineID and Dir over the stored row's, so the interest row names the current registration and every reader is correct unchanged. senderStamp, internal/session/handler.go:134,147, cmd/listener/durable.go:416-417, Registry.Match and internal/store/subject_index.go are left as they are.
specDepartures.evidence: Readers surviving the push deletion that read the first registration: internal/session/handler.go:134,147; cmd/listener/durable.go:416-417; internal/store/subject_index.go:40-84; Registry.Match (kv.go:1189-1195, called from delivery.go:980 and durable.go:387). Repointing senderStamp alone leaves the last three naming the first listener, and Registry.Match has no good repointing: dropping its machine argument re-adds the MatchAll that sjawhar/legion#2603 deletes, and rooting the index on the session entry means a 5-minute-TTL record (internal/session/registry.go:275) in a package store cannot import. Repointing also empties sender.Machine where no entry is written (cmd/listener/api.go:1511) and where the entry lapsed while the row lives (kv.go:1257-1263). internal/session/session.go:147-153 names this work. subjectIndex.set removes a key from its old root first (subject_index.go:44-59,62-77), and both writers pass the current machine id (api.go:1494-1498, kv.go:1018).

specDepartures.spec: A3: the grep "finds only the startup warning for the two variables and its test", excluding ':!**/CHANGELOG.md' ':!docs/solutions' ':!docs/plans' ':!docs/superpowers' ':!.superpowers'.
specDepartures.plan: The check adds ':!**/.changes/**', and adds ':!packages/claude-envoy/dist/**' for the pre-merge run only. Every one of the 61 files the command matches today is edited; the permitted residue is the warning in packages/envoy/cmd/listener/main.go and its test.
specDepartures.evidence: This repository's changelog fragments are packages/<pkg>/.changes/unreleased/*.yaml (root AGENTS.md, 'Changelog entries are fragment files'), which ':!**/CHANGELOG.md' does not exclude, and AGENTS.md requires a fragment for packages/envoy and packages/envoy-client; a fragment that tells an operator the two variables are gone would fail A3 as worded. packages/claude-envoy/dist/envoy-channel.js holds one hit bundled from packages/envoy-client/src/tool-contract.ts:198, which .github/workflows/claude-envoy-rebuild.yaml clears on main after the merge, which A3 already waits for.

acceptance: A3's command gains ':!**/.changes/**'; the pre-merge run also excludes packages/claude-envoy/dist/**.

specDepartures.spec: R1 lists the push code to delete and does not mention the Go renderer; A2 requires envoy-e2e-local to pass and is silent on the renderer assertions the script makes today.
specDepartures.plan: Deliverer.Text and foreignSession are deleted, with the nine golden assertions that call them and both sides of e2e-local.sh's Go-versus-TypeScript renderer comparison. The TypeScript renderInbound assertions over the captured envelopes stay.
specDepartures.evidence: Deliverer.Text (packages/envoy/internal/session/session.go:162-239) has exactly one non-test caller, Push (session.go:248); every other '.Text(' hit under packages/envoy is bufio.Scanner.Text, ast.CommentGroup.Text or a test. The script's Go side is built by parsing prompt.parts[].text out of the captured prompt_async bodies (scripts/e2e-local.sh:596-619) and asserted at :741-750, so it exists only because the push renders text server-side. With the push gone there is one renderer left, in packages/envoy-client, which has its own tests.

outcome.scope: Deleting Deliverer.Text, foreignSession, their nine golden tests (internal/session/session_test.go:348,364,383,405,424,442,475,524,859) and the Go half of the e2e renderer comparison is added to R1 and R3's work; cross-renderer parity coverage ends.

specDepartures.spec: R1: "the push-failed handling (pushFailedDeferrals and the push_failed reason in cmd/listener/unplaceable_delivery.go)".
specDepartures.plan: Neither name exists. The deletion is: the no_push_target reason and the unplaceable_no_push_target counter label (cmd/listener/unplaceable_delivery.go:182-187), session.ErrNoPushTarget (internal/session/session.go:44, produced at :144), and session.ReasonNoPushTarget and session.ReasonPushFailed (internal/session/handler.go:30-55). unplaceableDeferrals (unplaceable_delivery.go:101-110) and the no_session_record reason stay.
specDepartures.evidence: grep -rn 'pushFailedDeferrals\|push_failed' packages/envoy --include=*.go returns nothing. unplaceableDeferrals is keyed on stream sequence and is cause-agnostic (unplaceable_delivery.go:101-110,123-153), and the give-up path still serves ErrNoSessionRecord, so deleting it as R1 reads literally would delete live behaviour. No dashboard in this repository reads unplaceable_no_push_target: packages/envoy/infra/aws/metricfilter.go names no unplaceable label.

specDepartures.spec: A4: "The sender part fails on main with #2446 and INFRA-771 merged, before this change."
specDepartures.plan: The red baseline is main as it stands, with sjawhar/legion#2446 alone; the INFRA-771 precondition is dropped.
specDepartures.evidence: sjawhar/legion#2603 (dispatch://INFRA-771) is OPEN with 186 files, so no machine can run A4's baseline as worded today. #2603 keeps the mergeForUpsert pin verbatim and deletes none of the four surviving readers, so the sender assertions fail on main with or without it.

acceptance: A4's red baseline is main as it stands rather than main with INFRA-771 merged.
